title: Autoscaler alloc-token deadlock causing reserved-pool scaling stalls and customer burst shortfalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-burst period for several Dedicated customers this week, the autoscaler entered a deadlocked state in which allocation tokens were never released. Multiple reserved pools remained in "scaling" status for >15 minutes, preventing burst allocations and resulting in request throttling and elevated 429/503 rates for affected tenants. A high-severity escalation came from customer FinLedger who observed degraded throughput during peak end-of-month processing.

2026-03-01 02:45 UTC: Hotfix deployed to release a stale leader lease allowing allocator to reclaim tokens; partial capacity recovered for some pools.
2026-03-01 03:05 UTC: Full mitigation: autoscaler leader election code reverted to previous stable version while we prepare a thorough fix.
2026-03-01 04:00 UTC: Customer communications: notified affected tenants of partial mitigation and ETA for full fix.

steps_to_reproduce: Deploy autoscaler with leader-election enabled and a synthetic load that spawns 200 concurrent burst-surge requests across 15 reserved pools.
Simulate transient API datastore latency (~500ms) during alloc token check to trigger the race condition between token assignment and lease renewal.
Observe allocator logs for 'alloc-token: acquired but not released' and pool state stuck on 'scaling' beyond expected timeout.
Note that in this scenario, available GPU capacity exists but is not used because tokens are orphaned by deadlocked lease path.
root_cause: A race condition in the autoscaler leader-election / alloc-token lifecycle: when the allocator attempted to hand off tokens while also renewing the leader lease under transient datastore latency, it could mark tokens as 'assigned' without writing the corresponding release record under a failure path. This left tokens logically consumed while no active process held them, causing reserved pools to remain in an indeterminate 'scaling' state and blocking subsequent burst allocations.
investigation_notes: Log evidence shows 'token_acquire' events without matching 'token_release' across four distinct allocator pods during the incident window.
Datastore (lease table) had elevated p99 latency due to a transient table compaction running in the region; this increased the window for the race condition.

The new leader-election optimization merged two code paths (assign + renew) for latency reasons; it reduced steady-state latency but introduced a non-idempotent error path that wasn't fully tested under datastore latency.
Canary repro in staging successfully reproduced the stuck-token behavior when we injected datastore latency.
resolution: Merged PR #1442 which implements an idempotent token assignment protocol: writes a temporary transaction record before finalizing assignment and ensures a robust compensating release on partial failures. Added explicit token garbage-collection that detects tokens orphaned for >45s and returns them to the free pool. Released runtime-1.21 hotfix with monitoring and feature flag toggles.
rollback_steps: If regressions observed in canary/prod during rollout, flip feature flag to restore previous leader-election behavior and trigger GC job to reconcile tokens.

Automated rollback playbook: (1) disable new leader-election path via FF, (2) scale allocator deployment to 0 then back to desired replicas to force coordinator restart, (3) run token-reconciler job with dry-run -> apply mode.
Communicate rollback completion to SRE and affected customers.
runbook_updates: Add explicit healthcheck for 'orphaned-token-count' metric with alert threshold > 1 per region.
Document manual token-reconciliation steps and add a one-click runbook script accessible from Console -> Operations.
Increase autoscaler loop timeout metric visibility and add tracing for token lifecycle events.
monitoring_alerts: INC-AUTOSCALER-LOOP-LATENCY (existing) extended to include token-orphan delta

notes: This incident highlights a trade-off we made to reduce steady-state latency that reduced headroom for transient datastore issues. The fix keeps the latency wins but makes the error path safe and observable.
We should consider adding a canary that injects small datastore delays during nightly tests to prevent regressions of this class.
